newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon parliament dissolved ahead of poll.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon parliament dissolved ahead of poll.

text.p: Cameroon's parliament was dissolved after President Paul Biya rejected calls to extend its mandate following the postponement of legislative elections this month.
"This is a regrettable situation and a shame to Cameroon democracy," said MP Albert Dzonganga as he and other lawmakers left parliament after a last session on Saturday night.
He said the legislative vacuum would leave Biya with unlimited powers to govern because no new date had been set for the elections.
But deputy prime minister Gilbert Andze Tsoungui defended the government, saying that elections would be held in a matter of weeks. He gave no specific date.
"There is no problem," he said. "We can stay for some weeks without a National Assembly. There is nothing wrong with this."
Constitutionally elections should have been held last Sunday, a clear week before the expiry of parliament's mandate.
But a government decree on January 31 postponed the poll following opposition party complaints that their militants had not had enough time to register.

The government order said the aim was to prevent tension and street clashes that had characterised previous elections. It followed a stormy meeting between opposition leaders and government officials.

Tsoungui, who is in charge of territorial administration, said at the time that another reason for the postponement was to allow time to set up a constitutional council to proclaim results and deal with any complaints from candidates.

The election would be the second parliamentary poll since Cameroon's sometimes turbulent transition to multi-party democracy began in 1990. Part of the opposition boycotted the 1992 poll. Biya's supporters secured a majority then after allying with a minor party.
Biya, who took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982, faces a presidential election later this year.
